title: Salmon raises funds to double down in the Philippines
summary: Philippines-based banking and lending platform Salmon Group has raised $90 million in financing and another $50 million of bond proceeds.
content: Philippines-based banking and lending platform Salmon Group has successfully raised significant capital to expand its operations in the country. The company secured $90 million in financing along with an additional $50 million from bond proceeds. This fresh funding will enable Salmon to double down on its market strategy and further develop its financial services in the region.
content_ta: Philippines-வை தளமாகக் கொண்ட வங்கி மற்றும் கடன் வழங்கும் தளமான Salmon Group, தனது வணிகத்தை மேலும் விரிவுபடுத்துவதற்காக நிதி திரட்டியுள்ளது. இந்நிறுவனம் 90 மில்லியன் டாலர் நிதியுதவியையும், பத்திரங்கள் மூலம் கூடுதலாக 50 மில்லியன் டாலரையும் பெற்றுள்ளது. இந்த புதிய நிதி மூலம் Salmon தனது சந்தை உத்தியை வலுப்படுத்தி, அப்பகுதியில் தனது நிதி சேவைகளை மேலும் வளர்க்க முடியும்.

title: Stifel invests in Meow; preps white label treasury platform
summary: Stifel Financial has led a $31.6 million Series B finding round for business banking fintech Meow Technologies. The investment is part of a wider deal that will also see Stifel Bank offer a white-label version of Meow’s treasury management platform to its commercial banking clients.
content: Stifel Financial has led a $31.6 million Series B funding round for business banking fintech Meow Technologies. As part of the strategic investment, Stifel Bank will offer a white-label version of Meow's treasury management platform to its commercial banking clients, expanding financial services and banking technology capabilities.
content_ta: Stifel Financial நிறுவனம், பிசினஸ் பேங்கிங் ஃபின்டெக் நிறுவனமான Meow Technologies-க்கு $31.6 மில்லியன் சீரிஸ் B நிதி திரட்டலுக்கு தலைமை தாங்கியுள்ளது. இந்த முதலீட்டின் ஒரு பகுதியாக, Stifel Bank தனது வணிக வங்கிக் வாடிக்கையாளர்களுக்கு Meow-ன் கருவூல மேலாண்மை தளத்தின் ஒயிட்-லேபிள் பதிப்பை வழங்கவுள்ளது.

title: Katie Stockton Names 3 Warning Signs That Could Deepen the Stock Selloff
summary:
Fairlead's Katie Stockton names three warning signs, including wider credit spreads, that would deepen the stock selloff.
The post Katie Stockton Names 3 Warning Signs That Could Deepen the Stock Selloff appeared first on BeInCrypto.
content: Fairlead's Katie Stockton has identified three warning signs that could potentially deepen the ongoing stock market selloff. Among the key indicators highlighted is the widening of credit spreads. These technical signals provide critical insights for investors monitoring market volatility and economic conditions.
content_ta: Fairlead-ஐச் சேர்ந்த Katie Stockton, பங்குச் சந்தை சரிவை மேலும் ஆழப்படுத்தக்கூடிய மூன்று எச்சரிக்கை அறிகுறிகளைக் குறிப்பிட்டுள்ளார். கடன் பரவலில் ஏற்படும் விரிவாக்கம் உள்ளிட்ட முக்கிய குறிகாட்டிகள் இதில் சுட்டிக்காட்டப்பட்டுள்ளன. சந்தை நிலையற்ற தன்மையைக் கண்காணிக்கும் முதலீட்டாளர்களுக்கு இந்த எச்சரிக்கைகள் முக்கியமானதாக அமைகின்றன.

title: EU will ban cash payments over €10,000 starting July 2027
summary:
The EU's cash payment cap aims to curb illicit financial activities, impacting high-value transactions and necessitating stricter compliance measures.
The post EU will ban cash payments over €10,000 starting July 2027 appeared first on Crypto Briefing.
content: The European Union is set to implement a ban on cash payments exceeding €10,000 beginning in July 2027. This newly introduced cash payment cap is primarily designed to combat illicit financial activities across member states. The regulation will significantly impact high-value transactions and require businesses and consumers to adopt much stricter compliance measures moving forward.
content_ta: ஜூலை 2027 முதல் €10,000-க்கு மேற்பட்ட ரொக்கப் பணப் பரிவர்த்தனைகளுக்கு தடை விதிக்க EU திட்டமிட்டுள்ளது. சட்டவிரோத நிதி நடவடிக்கைகளைத் தடுப்பதை நோக்கமாகக் கொண்ட இந்த புதிய ரொக்கப் பரிவர்த்தனை வரம்பு, உயர் மதிப்புடைய பரிவர்த்தனைகளைப் பாதிக்கும் மற்றும் கடுமையான இணக்க நடவடிக்கைகளைக் கோரும்.

title: Nasdaq rises as AI and semiconductor stocks recover ahead of earnings
summary:
The Nasdaq's recovery highlights investor optimism, but upcoming earnings will test if AI and semiconductor growth can sustain amid economic pressures.
The post Nasdaq rises as AI and semiconductor stocks recover ahead of earnings appeared first on Crypto Briefing.
content: The Nasdaq index recently rose as artificial intelligence and semiconductor stocks staged a recovery. This upward movement reflects renewed investor optimism in the technology sector. However, upcoming corporate earnings reports will serve as a crucial test to determine whether the current growth momentum in AI and semiconductor markets can be sustained against broader economic pressures.
content_ta: Nasdaq இன்டெக்ஸ் சமீபத்தில் AI மற்றும் செமிகண்டக்டர் பங்குகள் மீண்டெழுந்ததால் உயர்ந்தது. இந்த மேல்நோக்கிய இயக்கம் தொழில்நுட்பத் துறையில் முதலீட்டாளர்களின் புதிய நம்பிக்கையைப் பிரதிபலிக்கிறது. இருப்பினும், வரவிருக்கும் கார்ப்பரேட் வருவாய் அறிக்கைகள், பரந்த பொருளாதார அழுத்தங்களுக்கு மத்தியில் AI மற்றும் செமிகண்டக்டர் சந்தைகளின் தற்போதைய வளர்ச்சி வேகத்தைத் தக்க வைத்துக் கொள்ள முடியுமா என்பதைத் தீர்மானிக்க ஒரு முக்கியமான சோதனையாக இருக்கும்.

title: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman outlines three endgames for AI development
summary:
The outlined AI development paths highlight potential risks of power centralization, necessitating global cooperation for balanced progress.
The post OpenAI CEO Sam Altman outlines three endgames for AI development appeared first on Crypto Briefing.
content: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman has outlined three potential endgames for artificial intelligence development. The discussion highlights the significant risks associated with the centralization of power in the tech industry. To ensure safe and balanced progress, Altman emphasizes the urgent need for global cooperation and careful navigation of future technological advancements.
content_ta: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, AI development-ன் மூன்று சாத்தியமான இறுதி நிலைகளை விளக்கியுள்ளார். தொழில்நுட்பத் துறையில் அதிகாரம் ஒரு இடத்திலேயே குவிக்கப்படுவதால் ஏற்படும் ஆபத்துகளை இது எடுத்துக்காட்டுகிறது. பாதுகாப்பான மற்றும் சீரான வளர்ச்சியை உறுதி செய்ய, உலகளாவிய ஒத்துழைப்பு மற்றும் எதிர்கால தொழில்நுட்ப முன்னேற்றங்களை கவனமாக கையாள்வது அவசியம் என்று அவர் வலியுறுத்துகிறார்.

title: CFTC secures more than $288 million order against former Long Island resident in Ponzi case
summary:
The ruling underscores the importance of due diligence for investors and reinforces regulatory efforts to deter financial misconduct.
The post CFTC secures more than $288 million order against former Long Island resident in Ponzi case appeared first on Crypto Briefing.
content: The CFTC has secured an order exceeding $288 million against a former Long Island resident involved in a Ponzi scheme. This significant legal action highlights ongoing regulatory crackdowns on fraudulent financial activities and emphasizes the critical need for investor due diligence to prevent heavy losses in deceptive investment schemes.
content_ta: Ponzi வழக்கில் தொடர்புடைய Long Island-ஐச் சேர்ந்த முன்னாள் நபர் மீது $288 மில்லியனுக்கும் அதிகமான தொகையை அபராதமாக செலுத்த CFTC உத்தரவிட்டுள்ளது. இந்த முக்கிய சட்ட நடவடிக்கை நிதி மோசடிகளுக்கு எதிரான ஒழுங்குமுறை நடவடிக்கைகளை வலுப்படுத்துவதோடு, முதலீட்டாளர்கள் கவனமுடன் இருக்க வேண்டியதன் அவசியத்தையும் வலியுறுத்துகிறது.

title: BNB Chain opens forum for community input on its new Layer 1
summary:
BNB Chain's NewL1 could redefine blockchain scalability and security, impacting trading, payments, and AI with its innovative features.
The post BNB Chain opens forum for community input on its new Layer 1 appeared first on Crypto Briefing.
content: BNB Chain has launched a new online forum to gather community feedback regarding its upcoming Layer 1 blockchain project. The initiative aims to involve developers and users in shaping the network, which promises to enhance blockchain scalability and security. This development could significantly impact various sectors, including digital trading, online payments, and artificial intelligence applications, as the project progresses toward deployment.
content_ta: BNB Chain தங்களது புதிய Layer 1 ப்ராஜெக்ட் குறித்த சமூகத்தின் கருத்துக்களைப் பெற ஒரு புதிய ஆன்லைன் மன்றத்தைத் தொடங்கியுள்ளது. பிளாக்செயின் அளவிடுதல் மற்றும் பாதுகாப்பை மேம்படுத்துவதை நோக்கமாகக் கொண்ட இந்த நெட்வொர்க்கை உருவாக்குவதில் டெவலப்பர்கள் மற்றும் பயனர்களை ஈர்ப்பதே இதன் நோக்கமாகும்.

title: Asia: Multilateral Lenders Advance Plans to Mobilise Private Capital, Expand Financing Capacity
summary: Multilateral development banks (MDBs) are stepping up efforts to attract private investment into emerging markets and increase their lending capacity as developing economies face mounting debt pressures, economic uncertainty, and climate-related disasters. The heads of the world’s major multilateral lenders met at the Asian Development... Read More
content: Major multilateral development banks are advancing plans to mobilize private capital and expand their financing capacity in emerging markets. Meeting in Asia, leaders of these institutions are responding to growing economic uncertainties, severe debt pressures, and climate-related disasters faced by developing economies, aiming to significantly boost investment and financial support.
content_ta: வளர்ந்து வரும் பொருளாதாரங்கள் எதிர்கொள்ளும் கடுமையான கடன் நெருக்கடிகள், பொருளாதார நிச்சயமற்ற தன்மைகள் மற்றும் பருவநிலை சார்ந்த பேரிடர்களைச் சமாளிக்க, முக்கிய MDBs தனியார் முதலீடுகளை ஈர்ப்பதற்கான திட்டங்களையும் தங்களின் நிதி வழங்கும் திறனை விரிவுபடுத்துவதற்கும் தீவிர நடவடிக்கைகளை எடுத்து வருகின்றன. ஆசியாவில் நடைபெற்ற இக்கூட்டத்தில், உலகின் முக்கிய பல்தரப்பு கடன் வழங்குநர்களின் தலைவர்கள் பங்கேற்றனர்.

title: Bitcoin rally could revive treasury buying, but easy-money days over
summary: “A return to last year’s indiscriminate capital raising looks unlikely,” said Bitfinex head of derivatives Jag Kooner.
content: A recent Bitcoin rally may encourage firms to resume treasury buying, though the era of easy money has ended. Analysts note that a return to last year's indiscriminate capital raising remains unlikely, indicating a more cautious approach to market expansion moving forward.
content_ta: சமீபத்திய Bitcoin விலை உயர்வு நிறுவனங்களை மீண்டும் கருவூல கொள்முதலில் ஈடுபடத் தூண்டலாம், இருப்பினும் எளிதான பண காலம் முடிவுக்கு வந்துவிட்டது. கடந்த ஆண்டைப் போல கண்மூடித்தனமாக நிதி திரட்டுவது இனி சாத்தியமில்லை என்றும், சந்தை விரிவாக்கத்தில் நிறுவனங்கள் மிகவும் எச்சரிக்கையுடன் செயல்படும் என்றும் ஆய்வாளர்கள் குறிப்பிடுகின்றனர்.

title: Binance opens free AI trading, yet user liability remains 100%
summary:
Standard includes 250,000 monthly usage credits and live deployment, while users must approve workflows and supply trading funds.
Read the full story on CryptoSlate
Understand the crypto stories that matter and what to watch next. Get The Catalyst in your inbox
content: Binance has launched a free AI trading tool offering monthly usage credits and live deployment capabilities. While the platform provides the technology, users must supply their own trading funds and approve workflows. Importantly, user liability remains completely with the individual, meaning traders assume full financial responsibility for any outcomes resulting from the automated strategies.
content_ta: Binance இலவச AI வர்த்தகக் கருவியை அறிமுகப்படுத்தியுள்ளது, இது மாதந்தோறும் பயன்பாட்டு வரம்புகளையும் நேரலை செயலாக்க வசதிகளையும் வழங்குகிறது. இந்தத் தொழில்நுட்பத்தை நிறுவனம் வழங்கினாலும், பயனர்கள் தங்களது சொந்த வர்த்தகப் பணத்தை முதலீடு செய்து பணிகளை அங்கீகரிக்க வேண்டும். மேலும், வர்த்தகங்களின் அனைத்து நிதிப் பொறுப்புகளும் முழுமையாகப் பயனர்களிடமே உள்ளது.

title: Cardano: Hoskinson reveals new programming language as ADA slips below $0.22
summary: Hoskinson outlined plans for a Cardano language that would combine users’ transaction requests with proof that their conditions were met.
content: Cardano founder Charles Hoskinson has revealed plans for a new programming language for the network. The proposed language aims to combine users' transaction requests with proof that their specific conditions are met. Meanwhile, the network's native token ADA experienced a price drop, slipping below the $0.22 mark amid broader market conditions.
content_ta: Cardano நிறுவனரான Charles Hoskinson, நெட்வொர்க்கிற்கான புதிய புரோகிராமிங் மொழி குறித்த திட்டங்களை வெளியிட்டுள்ளார். பயனர்களின் பரிவர்த்தனை கோரிக்கைகளை, அவர்களின் நிபந்தனைகள் பூர்த்தி செய்யப்படுவதற்கான ஆதாரத்துடன் இணைப்பதே இந்த புதிய மொழியின் நோக்கமாகும். இதற்கிடையில், நெட்வொர்க்கின் சொந்த கிரிப்டோகரன்சியான ADA விலை சரிந்து $0.22 என்ற அளவுக்கு கீழே சென்றது.

The digital asset trading platform announced that its registered user base has surpassed 62 million. During the month, Gate advanced its multi-asset trading, wealth management, and Web3 ecosystem services, demonstrating continued development across its diverse financial product offerings.
content_ta: Gate தனது செப்டம்பர் 2026 க்கான வெளிப்படைத்தன்மை அறிக்கையை வெளியிட்டது. உலகளாவிய பயனர் வளர்ச்சி மற்றும் வணிக விரிவாக்கம் இதில் சிறப்பிக்கப்பட்டுள்ளது. டிஜிட்டல் சொத்து வர்த்தக தளமான Gate-ன் பதிவு செய்யப்பட்ட பயனர்களின் எண்ணிக்கை 62 மில்லியனைக் கடந்துள்ளது. இந்த மாதத்தில், Gate தனது பல சொத்து வர்த்தக மற்றும் Web3 சுற்றுச்சூழல் சேரிப்புகளை மேலும் விரிவுபடுத்தியுள்ளது.

title: Why Citi Thinks Microsoft Beats Neoclouds in the AI Debt Squeeze
summary:
Citi's Tyler Radke blames bond yields, not weak demand, for the neocloud selloff and backs Microsoft instead.
The post Why Citi Thinks Microsoft Beats Neoclouds in the AI Debt Squeeze appeared first on BeInCrypto.
content: Citi analyst Tyler Radke believes that rising bond yields, rather than weak demand, are driving the recent selloff among neocloud providers. In light of the ongoing AI debt squeeze, Radke recommends Microsoft as a stronger and safer investment choice compared to independent neocloud companies navigating the challenging financial landscape.
content_ta: Citi-ன் ஆய்வாளரான Tyler Radke-ன் கூற்றுப்படி, neocloud நிறுவனங்களின் பங்குகள் சரிவுக்கு பலவீனமான தேவை காரணமல்ல, மாறாக உயர்ந்துவரும் பாண்ட் ஈவுத்தொகையே (bond yields) காரணம் ஆகும். தற்போதைய AI கடன் நெருக்கடியைச் சமாளிக்க, neocloud நிறுவனங்களை விட Microsoft சிறந்த மற்றும் பாதுகாப்பான முதலீட்டுத் தேர்வாக இருக்கும் என்று அவர் பரிந்துரைக்கிறார்.

title: KOSPI Falls 3.5% at Open as 2026 Gain Shrinks From 116% to 31%
summary:

The post KOSPI Falls 3.5% at Open as 2026 Gain Shrinks From 116% to 31% appeared first on BeInCrypto.
content: South Korea's KOSPI benchmark index experienced a significant drop, falling 3.5% at the market open. This sharp decline reduced its yearly gain for 2026 from 116% down to 31%. title: Zoho Launches Payroll Solution in the UK to Handle PAYE, National Insurance Calculations and RTI Submissions
summary:
Zoho Corporation, the global technology company, has launched Zoho Payroll, a payroll management solution built around the compliance requirements of UK businesses.
The solution handles Pay As You Earn (PAYE) and National Insurance calculations, as well as Real Time Information (RTI) submissions to HMRC. Zoho Payroll also comes with built-in AI capabilities, like Ask Zia Zoho's AI assistant tool, which payroll teams can use to complete tasks, generate forecasts and identify trends, using plain-language prompts. The AI assistant can also answer employees' payroll questions.
"Payroll is a critical component of the employee experience, so getting it right is important," said Prashant Ganti, VP of Global Product Strategy, Finance and Operations Business Unit, Zoho. "However, payroll doesn't happen in isolation, and because it shares sensitive employee data with other systems, any gap is a compliance risk and a privacy risk. Zoho Payroll offers built-in compliance, with privacy at its core, helping businesses always stay compliant as the rules evolve while keeping their employee data secure. Furthermore, the solution brings payroll, HR, employee expenses and accounting together in a smooth flow, so that businesses can pay their employees accurately and on time."
UK payroll is undergoing a significant period of regulatory change in recent years. Since April 2026, Statutory Sick Pay (SSP) is payable from the first day of sickness. More changes are expected to be implemented from April 2027 such as benefits in kind which must be taxed through payroll for each pay period instead of reporting it on P11D forms. Moreover, a full payment submission must be made to HMRC on or before payday, and late filing can attract monthly penalties starting at £100 for businesses with up to nine employees.
All these regulatory changes add to the existing compliance obligations of businesses making it more challenging for them to keep up. In fact, findings from a recent study done by Finity, show that 89% of payroll professionals said they had run into payment errors in the past year, and 38% said problems arise every month. Many of these avoidable errors stem from manual processes and disconnected systems, and this is the exact gap that Zoho Payroll is built to close.
The solution's key capabilities include:
● RTI reporting: a Full Payment Submission (FPS) generated for every pay run, and Employer Payment Summary (EPS) submissions where required.
● Statutory payments and deductions: All statutory payments such as Statutory Maternity Pay (SMP), Statutory Paternity Pay (SPP) and Statutory Sick Pay (SSP) based on employee eligibility can be managed seamlessly. The solution supports deductions like student loan repayments, Attachment of Earnings (AoE), Benefits in Kind (BiK), and P45 forms for employees leaving the organisation.
● Workplace pensions: businesses can run eligibility checks, auto-enrol eligible employees, handle opt-ins and opt-outs, and postpone pension enrolment when required.
● Payroll administration: employers can manage multiple work locations, with fine-grained role-based access, run activity logs, and set up payroll reminders
● Employee self-service: employees can review payslips, tax summaries and pension information through the self-service portal, available on web and mobile.
● Reporting: P11, P32 and payroll summary reports can be generated, and export them as PDF, XLS or CSV, with password-protected sharing.
Payroll, HR, employee expenses, and accounting in one connected flow

title: LHV Bank Goes Live With AI Agent for Customer Emails, Powered by Gradient Labs
summary:
LHV Bank has gone live with agentic AI for customer email support in the UK, powered by Gradient Labs. The launch follows a proof of concept announced earlier this year and means LHV’s retail customers can now get immediate answers to everyday banking questions by email, around the clock.
The AI agent handles common enquiries from start to finish, such as what to do about a lost card, an explanation of a payment, transfer queries, or what happens next with an existing request. Cases that are sensitive, complex or outside the agent’s approved procedures are passed to LHV’s customer support team.
Faster answers, more time for complex cases
Like other banks, LHV Bank's traditional queue-based approach to customer queries didn't distinguish between simple questions and complex ones. With this launch, simple queries get immediate answers, freeing up LHV's team to focus on the cases where human judgement matters most.
How it works
AI agent handles scoped journeys: Using Gradient Labs, LHV Bank's AI agent resolves clearly defined customer journeys from start to finish.
Works within set limits: The agent operates only within approved procedures, tools and controls.
Humans set the rules: LHV's teams define each process, its boundaries and what the agent is allowed to do.
Humans approve changes: Any updates are tested and signed off by LHV’s team before going live.
Ongoing oversight: LHV monitors quality and handles any exceptions the agent escalates.
Guardrails built for regulated banking
As LHV Bank operates in a regulated environment, its AI agent pairs large language models with deterministic guardrails. These control what data and tools the agent can access, when actions are blocked or escalated, and how complaints and vulnerable customers are handled. Customer data is never used to train the models, or build the agent, and is accessed only during live interactions.
Improving the agent like software
LHV Bank is also using Collaborate, part of the Gradient Labs platform, which applies software engineering discipline to customer-facing AI. LHV’s operations, product, engineering, risk and compliance teams can draft changes to the agent’s procedures in a controlled branch, test them against representative customer cases, review and approve them before they reach customers, and roll them back if needed. Every change carries a clear record of what changed, who approved it and when, so the service can improve continuously without the bank losing control of it.
What’s next?
LHV Bank’s immediate focus is to extend the agent to more customer servicing procedures within UK email support. Longer term, the two companies will explore further channels such as live chat and voice, back-office and financial crime workflows including onboarding, KYC and AML, and potential expansion into LHV’s Estonian business.
Kris Brewster, Interim CEO of LHV Bank, comments:



Dimitri Masin, CEO of Gradient Labs, added: 
“The future of AI in financial services is not a faster human approving AI suggestions at every step. It is trusted agents taking responsibility for defined work, supported by deterministic controls, clear escalation points and human judgement where it matters. LHV is showing what that can look like in practice.”

title: New Research Shows How AI Will Change the Gift Card Industry
summary:
Blackhawk Network (BHN), a global branded payments leader, today released new research surveying 694 U.S. business leaders responsible for incentives, commerce and branded payments, finding that artificial intelligence could fundamentally change how consumers discover, select and purchase gift cards. The findings are pertinent as businesses prepare for a future where AI assistants will act on a shopper’s behalf.
 
According to BHN's AI & Branded Payments Study, 42% of the payments leaders surveyed believe that by 2030, AI will most likely reshape consumers' path to purchasing gift cards through an AI concierge. This assistant will recommend a gift card, select the value and send it—without the consumer ever visiting the retailer's website or app. Another 32% expect AI will recommend gift cards based on a recipient's interests, past purchases and preferences, while 24% expect AI assistants to purchase and deliver the right gift card for preapproved occasions.
 

“AI has the potential to change not only how consumers find the right gift, but how that purchase ultimately gets made,” said Talbott Roche, CEO and president of BHN. “As AI assistants take a more active role in shopping, brands will need to consider how they remain discoverable, relevant and connected to customers when agents are helping determine what gets purchased.”
 
Businesses are already beginning to prepare for that shift. Twenty-three percent of the payments leaders surveyed said they are building or piloting for agentic commerce, while another 47% are actively exploring what it means for their branded payments programs. Twenty-two percent are aware of agentic commerce but have not yet taken action, while just 8% said they are not thinking about it yet.
 
The findings suggest AI could also emerge as a new distribution channel for branded payments. Additionally, AI will more effectively integrate gift cards into shoppers’ lives. For instance, an AI assistant could surface an existing gift card when a consumer is shopping at a relevant retailer, or proactively suggest an appropriate gift card and budget for an upcoming loved one’s special occasion. As AI assistants become capable of moving consumers from recommendation to purchase within a single interaction, brands will need to make gift cards and stored value easier for AI systems to find, understand and confidently recommend.
 

“For brands, the broader opportunity is to make stored value more useful in the moments when consumers are ready to act, while still giving them transparency and control over the experience,” Roche said.
 
Thirty-five percent of businesses surveyed also identified customer experience as an area where they expect AI to have the greatest impact on branded payments by 2030. The research found businesses are looking for better data and analytics and more personalized gifting experiences as they consider how to put AI to work within their programs.
 
Download BHN’s AI & Branded Payments Study here.
 

*BHN’s U.S. AI & Branded Payments Study was an online survey conducted between April and June 2026. The sample included 694 respondents responsible for incentives, commerce and branded payments.

title: BlackRock Files For Bitcoin ETF With Managed Downside Protection
summary: TL;DR: BlackRock has proposed another Bitcoin-linked ETF, this time using options to pursue some protection against losses while giving up part of the potential upside. BlackRock’s latest Bitcoin fund filing takes a different approach from the familiar buy-and-hold exposure offered by its iShares Bitcoin Trust. Instead of simply following the price of Bitcoin, the proposed iShares Bitcoin Managed Protection ETF would use an options strategy linked to IBIT or similar exposure. The ambition is straightforward enough: participate in some of Bitcoin’s gains and seek a measure of protection during a decline. The trade-off is equally important. Gains could be capped, and the protection is neither unconditional nor guaranteed. The structure is designed around overlapping options positions, meaning an investor’s outcome could depend on when the shares are purchased as well as what Bitcoin does next. That makes this a different kind of product, not a safer version of holding spot Bitcoin in every circumstance. Options costs, fund expenses and changing market prices all affect what shareholders receive. The filing arrives as issuers work to move beyond basic spot exposure. Income-oriented and buffered Bitcoin products try to give financial advisers additional ways to fit an unusually volatile asset into conventional portfolios. For investors, the missing details matter as much as the proposed strategy. An SEC filing does not mean the fund has been approved or launched. Its eventual fees, live portfolio and actual protection terms will determine whether the structure delivers a useful alternative to IBIT. Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.
content: BlackRock has filed an SEC application for a new Bitcoin ETF featuring managed downside protection. Unlike traditional buy-and-hold spot funds, the proposed iShares Bitcoin Managed Protection ETF would use an options strategy to limit potential losses while also capping gains during market downturns. The product aims to help advisers integrate Bitcoin into conventional portfolios, though it awaits regulatory approval and final pricing details.

title: Two in Five Financial Services Leaders Say AI Capability Gaps Have Cost Them Business
summary:
​​​Two in five (40%) financial services directors and C-Suite professionals say their organisation has lost a competitive bid or client opportunity partly because of AI capability concerns, according to new research from Kaplan UK - a leading provider of professional education, apprenticeship training, and enterprise upskilling.
The findings suggest that capability gaps are beginning to have a direct commercial impact in a sector where AI adoption is already a significant strategic priority.
More than four in five (81%) C-Suite respondents in financial services told Kaplan that AI adoption and expansion is a high or top organisational priority over the next 12 months, compared with 74% of leaders across industries overall.
Financial services C-Suite teams were also more likely to say they are confident their organisation has a clearly defined AI strategy that is understood at senior level.
However, Kaplan’s research suggests investment in the sector remains more heavily weighted towards technology than the workforce expected to use it.
Half (50%) of financial services C-Suite respondents said their organisation has placed greater emphasis on investing in AI tools and technology, compared with just 17% who said greater emphasis has been placed on workforce capability development.
The findings are published in Kaplan’s new whitepaper, From AI to ROI: Who owns the problem? which examines the relationship between AI investment, workforce capability and business performance. The Kaplan study is grounded in the views of 1,000 UK employees, 600 HR and L&D professionals, and 600 company directors and C-Suite leaders.
Financial services leaders also estimated that fewer than half of the employees (45%) expected to work with AI are genuinely proficient, compared to 79% of employees in the sector that are confident in using AI productively.
Taken together, the findings point to a potential gap between strategic ambition and organisations’ ability to translate AI investment into day-to-day capability. Despite high levels of leadership focus on AI, many financial services businesses are investing more heavily in the technology itself than in developing the people expected to apply it.
​​​Chiraag Swaly, Head of Data and Technology Curriculum at Kaplan, said: “Financial services organisations clearly recognise the strategic importance of AI. The sector is prioritising adoption and leaders are putting AI strategies in place, but the research suggests that technology investment alone is not enough to generate a return.
“When four in ten C-Suite leaders say AI capability concerns have contributed to losing a bid or client opportunity, workforce capability becomes a commercial issue rather than simply a training issue.
“Financial services employees operate in environments where judgement, accuracy and the appropriate use of technology matter enormously. Giving people access to AI is therefore only one part of the challenge. Organisations also need to ensure employees can apply those tools effectively in the context of their roles.
“The gap between investment in technology and investment in workforce capability is significant. Closing it will require organisations to treat the skills needed to use AI as part of the transformation itself, rather than something that follows deployment.”
The findings reflect a broader pattern identified by Kaplan across UK businesses. While organisations are investing heavily in AI, the research suggests workforce development is not always progressing at the same pace.
Across industries, 54% of C-Suite and director respondents said AI-related investment has placed greater emphasis on tools and technology than workforce capability development, while only 20% say the greater emphasis has been on developing employees’ skills.
Kaplan argues that the challenge for financial services organisations is therefore not simply to accelerate AI adoption, but to ensure investment in technology is matched by the practical capability needed to use it effectively across the workforce.

title: Xceptor Expands Investment in Japan to Help Financial Institutions Modernise Capital Markets Operations
summary:
Xceptor, a global leader in data automation for capital markets, today announced it has expanded its investment in Japan to help more financial institutions transform their operating models and drive domestic and international growth.
Xceptor has already established a strong presence in the region, including the launch of its sovereign-grade SaaS offering and strategic partnership with GRCS for local implementation. A Japanese megabank recently selected Xceptor and GRCS to implement Xceptor's SaaS platform, streamlining fragmented post-trade workflows and building a foundation for future innovation.  Xceptor now partners with two of Japan's three megabanks.
As part of its commitment to Japan, Xceptor has appointed Airi Iwamoto as Key Account Director and Satomi Hirono as Principal, Client Success. Both will focus on helping Japanese firms, from large banks to commodities houses (Sogo Shosha), automate mission-critical post-trade processes such as affirmations, confirmations, end-user computing (EUC) remediation, and fund services. Region-specific product capabilities, such as a Japanese-language user interface (UI), are also being rolled out to enable easier adoption and enhance the user experience.
“Many Japanese financial institutions rely on a significant number of disconnected EUC applications and manual processes developed around core banking systems,” said Keith Man, General Manager, APAC at Xceptor. “Any update to a core platform requires extensive testing for each application, adding risk while slowing transformation and AI adoption.”
“Japan’s megabanks are reshaping their Corporate and Investment Banking (CIB) businesses to accelerate global growth,” added Keith Man. “Xceptor already partners with many of the world’s largest banks, and more Japanese firms are looking to draw on our experience to help them on that journey. I’m delighted to welcome Airi and Satomi to the team as we expand our presence in the region.”

title: Bitcoin ETF comeback exposes a $630 million divide with Ethereum as BlackRock dominates
summary: TL;DR: BlackRock’s IBIT recorded roughly $665 million in net inflows on October 19, even as several other US spot Bitcoin ETFs saw investors take money out. A strong day for Bitcoin ETFs wasn’t quite as broad-based as the headline number suggests. BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust took in approximately $665.16 million on Monday, according to SoSoValue’s fund-flow figures, while the US spot Bitcoin ETF group recorded a combined inflow of about $526.6 million. That difference is the story. Money going into IBIT more than offset withdrawals from competing funds. Fidelity’s FBTC registered roughly $83.6 million in outflows, while Grayscale’s GBTC shed about $54.9 million. Rather than a uniform surge of demand for every Bitcoin product, Monday’s numbers point to a preference for the market’s biggest vehicle. IBIT has become the default choice for many investors seeking exchange-traded Bitcoin exposure, although a single day’s figures cannot establish why individual institutions moved money. The reversal also follows a Friday session in which the group recorded net withdrawals. It underscores how quickly flows can shift around market volatility and broader risk sentiment. Flows are useful evidence of ETF subscriptions and redemptions, but they shouldn’t be read as a direct measure of new cash buying Bitcoin at a particular hour. Fund mechanics and market-making activity complicate that picture. The next question is whether demand spreads to other products or whether IBIT continues to absorb most of the market’s incremental interest. Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.
content: BlackRock's IBIT dominated the Bitcoin ETF market with massive net inflows of over $660 million, offsetting withdrawals from competing funds like Fidelity's FBTC and Grayscale's GBTC. While the overall US spot Bitcoin ETF group saw positive inflows, the data highlights a growing market divide as investors increasingly favor BlackRock's dominant product amid shifting risk sentiment.

title: Visa And Mesh Want Crypto Wallet Balances To Work At 175 Million Merchants
summary: TL;DR: Mesh and Visa have announced a partnership intended to let consumers spend cryptocurrency and stablecoins from participating wallet apps wherever Visa payments are accepted. Holding stablecoins is one thing. Actually spending them in a shop usually involves moving funds to an exchange, selling them, or relying on a separate payment product. Visa and Mesh are pitching a way to make that process less visible to the customer. Under their newly announced partnership, Mesh’s payment infrastructure will connect eligible crypto wallet balances with Visa’s acceptance network, spanning more than 175 million merchant locations. The ambition is to support both online and in-person spending without requiring customers to manually cash out their tokens first. Visa supplies the acceptance infrastructure. Mesh provides the orchestration layer responsible for connecting wallet balances to a payment made in the currency a merchant expects to receive. It’s a potentially significant distribution arrangement for digital asset payments, but the announcement is not the same as saying every crypto wallet already works in every shop. Participating apps, market availability and the precise rollout remain important variables. For merchants, the appeal is continuity: they would interact with an established payments network rather than needing to accept a particular blockchain asset directly. For wallet providers, the attraction is a more everyday use for balances that often stay within crypto trading platforms. The test will be whether the experience is genuinely as simple as a conventional card payment once the integration reaches customers. Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.
content: Visa and Mesh have announced a partnership to allow consumers to spend cryptocurrency and stablecoins directly from participating wallet apps at more than 175 million merchant locations worldwide. The collaboration uses Visa's acceptance network alongside Mesh's payment infrastructure, aiming to enable seamless online and in-person spending without the need for customers to manually cash out their digital tokens beforehand.

title: Mastercard Introduces Risk Intelligence to Enable More Secure Stablecoin Payments
summary:
Today at Money20/20 USA, Mastercard announced Stablecoin Security, a new risk intelligence solution, with Borderless.xyz and Keyrails as initial partners. As stablecoins play a growing role in cross-border and business-to-business payments, financial institutions need a clearer view of risk across increasingly complex payment flows. The solution builds on Mastercard’s existing capabilities and helps financial institutions identify fraud, scams, sanctions and other financial-crime risk indicators throughout the stablecoin payment lifecycle, including before funds move on-chain.
Why do financial institutions need better stablecoin risk intelligence? 
A study of 593 million stablecoin transfer events across 141 million Ethereum transactions in 2025 found that nearly 60% were complex, multi-step transactions, rather than simple, one-to-one payments. This can make it harder for financial institutions to assess risk across the full payment journey, from supplier payments and global trade settlement to moving funds across countries and currencies. Stablecoin Security helps close that gap by combining payment intelligence with blockchain analytics, giving financial institutions a more complete view of risk at key points in the transaction lifecycle.
“Stablecoins are creating new possibilities for value exchange, but financial institutions need the right intelligence and controls to participate with confidence,” said Ann Johnson, executive vice president, Security Solutions at Mastercard. “By bringing payment and blockchain insights together, Stablecoin Security extends Mastercard’s fraud and risk capabilities to digital asset payments, giving institutions a clearer view of risk to make more informed decisions and build greater trust.”
How does Stablecoin Security work? 
Delivered through a platform-agnostic application programming interface (API), Stablecoin Security analyzes signals including transaction context, where the funds came from, exposure to restricted parties and scam indicators. It generates intelligence across the fiat and stablecoin payment lifecycle, including a risk score before a payment is completed, and can be integrated into existing fraud, compliance and case management workflows. This allows financial institutions to support stablecoin payments without creating a separate risk operating model.
For example, consider a coffee shop owner in Boston purchasing coffee beans from a supplier in Brazil. The coffee shop initiates payment through its bank, which uses stablecoins to move funds across borders more quickly and efficiently. Before the payment is sent, the bank’s service provider uses Mastercard Stablecoin Security to analyze payment and blockchain intelligence, helping the bank determine whether the payment can proceed as expected or should be reviewed further. The Brazilian supplier receives the funds and confidently converts the stablecoin to local currency.
Partnering across the stablecoin ecosystem to scale 
Mastercard is working with Borderless.xyz and Keyrails, both participants in Mastercard’s Start Path Blockchain and Digital Assets startup engagement program, to bring Stablecoin Security to real-world payment flows. Keyrails supports high-value cross-border trade payments, particularly in emerging markets. Borderless.xyz gives financial institutions a single connection to licensed stablecoin providers in more than 113 countries and 72 currencies, handles the operations behind every payment, and enables routing each one to the best provider. In 2027, Mastercard will continue to expand Stablecoin Security’s reach and adoption, including through BVNK, the stablecoin infrastructure provider it acquired in August 2026.
Stablecoin Security builds on Mastercard's broader efforts to bring trust, security and transparency to stablecoin and digital asset transactions. Alongside complementary capabilities such as Mastercard Crypto Credential and Crypto Secure, it aims to help financial institutions navigate emerging forms of money movement with greater confidence. 
The solution is launching first in North America, with commercial availability expected worldwide in 2027.

title: Salmon Secures $140 Million (PHP 8.8 Billion) to Double Down on the Growth Opportunity in the Philippines
summary:
Salmon Group, a technology-driven banking and lending platform in the Philippines, today announces that it secured additional $140 million of financing to continue its growth in the Philippines.
Proceeds from the financing round will fund the scaling of profitable lending (Salmon Credit Line and in-store lending) and nationwide roll-out of new products, including motorcycle and MSME lending.
In less than four years of operations, Salmon has become one of the fastest-growing technology companies in the Philippines, operating through a BSP-licensed bank, Salmon Bank (Rural Bank) and an SEC-licensed financing company, Salmon Finance.  
Today, the companies in Salmon Group serve millions of Filipinos through its Salmon app – one of the highest rated financial services apps in the Philippines with 9 million downloads, 4.8 rating on App Store and Google Play, 99.9% uptime, and dedicated 24/7 customer support.  Through the AI-powered credit engine of Salmon Finance, the group's financing arm, Salmon is able to serve customers with limited credit history and provide credit decisions within minutes.
"Everyday financial services come with unnecessary friction for many Filipinos.  We're removing these barriers and building innovative products with the reliability and security customers expect in today's world," said Pavel Fedorov, co-founder of Salmon. "We are doubling down on the opportunity in the Philippines as we believe deeply in its scale and in the importance of focus to deliver a differentiated execution.  This financing lets us do more: extend banking and credit access to more Filipinos, roll out new products, and keep raising the bar for the financial services industry in the country. We are grateful to our existing investors for backing the next stage of our mission."

title: AutoRek Supports Leading UK Digital Investment Platforms as Demand for Automated Reconciliation Grows

By automating processes that have traditionally relied heavily on manual intervention, firms can build a stronger operational foundation as their businesses continue to grow.”
The two customer wins reflect a broader shift across the UK digital investment sector, where platforms are increasingly focused on improving the scalability and resilience of their operating models. AutoRek's technology provides automated matching, break management and configurable financial controls designed to support organisations as transaction volumes and operational complexity increase.
The new relationships build on AutoRek's growing presence across the financial services sector, where it works with organisations to automate critical reconciliation and financial control processes.

title: August Breaks UK Credit Card Record as Balances Soar
summary:
According to data analysis from global analytics software leader FICO, average active UK credit card balances exceeded £2,000 in August for the first time since records began, following three consecutive months of increases. Contributing to higher balances, payment rates dropped after a brief recovery in July, and remain lower than the same time last year. This trend, coupled with an annual increase in all levels of missed payments, highlights the importance of risk teams continuing to closely monitor for signs of financial difficulty.
Highlights
Average spending increased by 3.1% month-on-month to £840, growing 3.3% year-on-year and marking the highest annual growth rate in over a year.
The average active balance grew 1.2% month-on-month to a record £2,005 and remains up 4.8% year-on-year.
The percentage of overall balance paid fell 1.1% on the previous month, to 33.3%, and is down 3.1% year-on-year.
Average credit limits crossed £6,000 for the first time, and overlimit accounts grew 4.7% month-on-month to an average overlimit of £95. This is down -3.1% on the previous month but up 3.3% year-on-year.
The percentage of customers missing one payment fell by 7.1% month-on-month but balances for these accounts rose 5.1% year-on-year, to £2,520.
Accounts with two missed payments climbed 2.8% compared to July, but are 9.5% higher year-on-year. Annual growth for balances of these accounts slowed to 1.8%, with the average standing at £2,945.
There was a slight monthly decline of 0.7% in three missed payments, but year-on-year there was a sharp increase of 16.4%. Average balances grew 1.7% on the year, reaching £3,320.
FICO Comment:
August marked significant milestones, as average active balances passed £2,000 and credit limits exceeded £6,000 for the first time. The year-on-year shortfall in payment rates narrowed for a third consecutive month, while overlimit accounts showed year-on-year improvement. This suggests that acute affordability pressures from earlier in the year are beginning to ease slightly, despite the persistent pressure on finances that has characterised the market since early 2025. However, late payments across all three cycles remain higher than in 2025, reflecting a macroeconomic environment that continues to stretch household budgets.
UK CPI inflation rose to 3.1% in August, up from 2.9% in July, driven in part by rising food prices. With Ofgem’s energy price cap set to increase, borrowing costs are unlikely to fall significantly before winter. Meanwhile, total UK credit card debt has reached a record £82.4 billion according to the Bank of England, alongside record-high representative credit card interest rates.
Given these cost pressures, risk teams should monitor whether the recent stability in payment rates and overlimit accounts can be sustained. Although one-cycle delinquency fell sharply in August, it remains 5.1% higher year-on-year. As the primary entry point to the delinquency pipeline, and with CPI and energy costs both rising into autumn, early intervention and tailored support for this population should be prioritised before further seasonal pressure builds

content: UK credit card balances exceeded £2,000 for the first time in August, according to FICO data, driven by rising spending and falling payment rates. Average credit limits also crossed £6,000. While some affordability pressures eased slightly, missed payments remained higher year-on-year amid ongoing economic challenges, including rising inflation and energy costs.
content_ta: FICO-வின் தரவுகளின்படி, ஆகஸ்ட் மாதத்தில் UK-ல் கிரெடிட் கார்டு நிலுவைத் தொகைகள் முதல்முறையாக £2,000-ஐத் தாண்டின. அதிகரித்த செலவினங்களும் குறைந்த செலுத்தல் விகிதங்களும் இதற்குக் காரணமாகும். சராசரி கிரெடிட் வரம்புகளும் £6,500-ஐத் தாண்டியுள்ளன. பொருளாதார சவால்கள் தொடரும் நிலையில், கட்டணம் செலுத்தத் தவறியவர்களின் எண்ணிக்கை சென்ற ஆண்டைக் காட்டிலும் அதிகமாகவே உள்ளது.

title: Microsoft, Alphabet and Goldman Sachs join objections to OKX-ICE tokenized stock trading
summary: Seven more issuers have opted out of being listed on the planned tokenized stock venue under the SEC's framework, bringing its disclosed objection count to 16.
content: Microsoft, Alphabet, and Goldman Sachs are among seven new issuers joining objections to the planned OKX-ICE tokenized stock trading venue. This brings the total number of disclosed objections to 16 under the current regulatory framework.
content_ta: திட்டமிடப்பட்ட OKX-ICE டோக்கனைஸ்டு பங்கு வர்த்தக தளத்திற்கு எதிரான எதிர்ப்புகளில் Microsoft, Alphabet மற்றும் Goldman Sachs உள்ளிட்ட ஏழு புதிய நிறுவனங்கள் இணைந்துள்ளன. இதன் மூலம் தற்போதைய ஒழுங்குமுறை கட்டமைப்பின் கீழ் மொத்த எதிர்ப்புகளின் எண்ணிக்கை 16 ஆக உயர்ந்துள்ளது.

title: Agents can trade 24/7 — but Yat Siu warns you could lose access at any time
summary: The Animoca Brands chairman explains that AI agents can make trades while you sleep, but users need to plan for the day they lose access to the bots.
content: Animoca Brands chairman Yat Siu warns that while AI agents can trade 24/7 around the clock, users must prepare for potential disruptions. Although automated bots allow for continuous overnight trading, investors face the risk of suddenly losing access to their accounts and should plan ahead for such technological failures.
content_ta: AI ஏஜெண்டுகள் 24 மணி நேரமும் வர்த்தகம் செய்ய முடியும் என்றாலும், எப்போது வேண்டுமானாலும் அணுகலை இழக்க நேரிடும் என்று Animoca Brands நிறுவனத்தின் தலைவர் Yat Siu எச்சரித்துள்ளார். தானியங்கி பாட்கள் மூலம் தொடர்ந்து வர்த்தகம் செய்ய முடிந்தாலும், பயனர்கள் கணக்குகளுக்கான அணுகலை திடீரென இழக்கும் அபாயத்தை எதிர்கொள்வதோடு, அத்தகைய சூழ்நிலைகளுக்கு முன்கூட்டியே திட்டமிட வேண்டும்.

title: Drift exploiter sends $61M ETH to Tornado Cash, holds $194M
summary: The April 1 hack caused about $295 million in losses and was later attributed to a North Korean threat group in a Mandiant investigation.
content: The exploiter behind the Drift protocol hack transferred $61 million in ETH to Tornado Cash, while still holding $194 million. The April 1 security breach resulted in approximately $295 million in total losses. A subsequent investigation by Mandiant attributed the cyberattack to a North Korean threat group.
content_ta: Drift புரோட்டோகால் ஹேக் சம்பவத்துடன் தொடர்புடைய ஹேக்கர், $61 மில்லியன் மதிப்புள்ள ETH-ஐ Tornado Cash-க்கு மாற்றியுள்ளார், மேலும் அவரிடம் இன்னும் $194 மில்லியன் உள்ளது. கடந்த ஏப்ரல் 1 அன்று நடந்த இந்த பாதுகாப்பு மீறலால் சுமார் $295 மில்லியன் இழப்பு ஏற்பட்டது. Mandiant நடத்திய விசாரணையில், இந்த சைபர் தாக்குதலுக்கு வட கொரியாவைச் சேர்ந்த ஹேக்கர் குழு காரணம் என்பது தெரியவந்துள்ளது.

title: Tx launches USTX stablecoin to pull RWA liquidity onto its chain
summary: The Brale-issued token can be minted with USDC from eight networks and is designed to settle tokenized stocks and other assets on tx.
content: Tx has launched the USTX stablecoin, issued by Brale, to bring real-world asset liquidity onto its blockchain. The new token can be minted using USDC across eight different networks. It is specifically designed to facilitate the settlement of tokenized stocks and other digital assets directly on the Tx network.
content_ta: RWA லிக்யூடிட்டியை தனது நெட்வொர்க்கிற்கு கொண்டு வருவதற்காக Tx பிளாட்ஃபார்ம் Brale-இன் வெளியீடான USTX ஸ்டேபிள்காயினை அறிமுகப்படுத்தியுள்ளது. இந்த புதிய டோக்கனை எட்டு நெட்வொர்க்குகளில் உள்ள USDC உதவியுடன் மிண்ட் செய்ய முடியும். Tx நெட்வொர்க்கில் டோக்கனைஸ்டு பங்குகள் மற்றும் பிற சொத்துகளின் பரிவர்த்தனைகளை எளிதாக்கும் வகையில் இது வடிவமைக்கப்பட்டுள்ளது.

title: Lloyds and Barclays among UK banks named in crypto transfer complaints, advocacy group says

content_ta: Lloyds மற்றும் Barclays உள்ளிட்ட UK வங்கிகள் crypto பரிமாற்ற வரம்புகள் மற்றும் தடைகள் தொடர்பான கடுமையான கண்காணிப்பை எதிர்கொண்டு வருகின்றன. Stand With Crypto என்ற ஆர்வலர் குழுவின்படி, UK-இன் வரவிருக்கும் 2027 ஒழுங்குமுறை விதிமுறைக்கு முன்னதாக வாடிக்கையாளர்களிடமிருந்து ஆயிரக்கணக்கான புகார்கள் வந்துள்ளன.

content_ta: Blockchain.com நிறுவனம் தனது பயனர்களுக்காக புதிய கிரிப்டோகரன்சி ஆப்ஷன்ஸ் வர்த்தகத்தை அறிமுகப்படுத்தியுள்ளது. இதில் BTC, ETH, SOL, HYPE, AVAX, XRP மற்றும் TRX உள்ளிட்ட பிரபல டிஜிட்டல் சொத்துக்கள் ஒரு வாரம் வரை காலாவதியாகும் காலகட்டத்துடன் சேர்க்கப்பட்டுள்ளன. அமெரிக்காவில் டெரிவேட்டிவ்களுக்கான உரிமங்களைப் பெறும் முயற்சியின் ஒரு பகுதியாக இந்த புதிய சேவை விரிவுபடுத்தப்பட்டுள்ளது.

title: Stablecoins move over $400 million per hour on average as off-hours transfers dominate, Coinbase and The Block study finds
summary: Stablecoins are on track to reach $1.5 trillion in quarterly adjusted transfer volume by the end of 2027 at current growth rates, according to the report.
content: A new study by Coinbase and The Block reveals that stablecoins process over $400 million per hour on average, with off-hours transfers dominating activity. At current growth rates, quarterly adjusted transfer volume for stablecoins is projected to reach $1.5 trillion by the end of 2027.
content_ta: Coinbase மற்றும் The Block நடத்திய புதிய ஆய்வின்படி, Stablecoins சராசரியாக மணிக்கு $400 மில்லியனுக்கும் அதிகமான பரிவர்த்தனைகளைக் கையாள்கின்றன, இதில் பணி நேரத்திற்கு வெளியே செய்யப்படும் பரிவர்த்தனைகளே அதிகம். தற்போதைய வளர்ச்சி விகிதத்தின்படி, Stablecoins-களின் காலாண்டு சரிசெய்யப்பட்ட பரிவர்த்தனை அளவு 2027 ஆம் ஆண்டின் இறுதிக்குள் $1.5 டிரில்லியனை எட்டும் என்று எதிர்பார்க்கப்படுகிறது.

title: Crypto wallet security crisis deepens as NGRAVE users face $2.65 million phishing attack
summary:

Read the full story on CryptoSlate
Understand the crypto stories that matter and what to watch next. Get The Catalyst in your inbox
content: A major cryptocurrency wallet security crisis has deepened following a phishing attack targeting NGRAVE users, resulting in losses estimated at $2.65 million. Blockchain analytics firm Bitquery tracked some of the stolen funds into XMR purchases on Hyperliquid, though investigators could not independently verify if every involved wallet strictly belonged to an NGRAVE user. The incident highlights ongoing security vulnerabilities within the digital asset ecosystem.
content_ta: NGRAVE யூசர்களை குறிவைத்து நடத்தப்பட்ட பிஷிங் தாக்குதல் காரணமாக கிரிப்டோவாலெட் பாதுகாப்பு நெருக்கடி மேலும் தீவிரமடைந்துள்ளது. இந்தத் தாக்குதலில் தோராயமாக $2.65 மில்லியன் மதிப்புள்ள சொத்துக்கள் இழக்கப்பட்டுள்ளன. திருடப்பட்ட நிதியில் சில பகுதிகள் Hyperliquid-ல் XMR வாங்குவதற்கு பயன்படுத்தப்பட்டதை Bitquery பிளாக்சைன் நிறுவன பகுப்பாய்வாளர்கள் கண்டறிந்துள்ளனர். இருப்பினும், சம்பந்தப்பட்ட அனைத்து வாலெட்டுகளும் NGRAVE யூசர்களை மட்டுமே சேர்ந்தவை என்பதை முழுமையாக உறுதிப்படுத்த முடியவில்லை.

title: Sam Callahan: Bitcoin Doesn’t Need Rate Cuts to Succeed
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Sam Callahan: Bitcoin Doesn’t Need Rate Cuts to Succeed
The USD lost 20% purchasing power in 5 years. Sam Callahan breaks down financial repression, core PCE spikes, and the U.S. bond market's historic drawdown.
This post Sam Callahan: Bitcoin Doesn’t Need Rate Cuts to Succeed first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Patrick Green.
content: Bitcoin analyst Sam Callahan argues that Bitcoin does not require interest rate cuts from the Federal Reserve to succeed. In a recent analysis, Callahan discussed ongoing financial repression, core PCE spikes, and a historic drawdown in the U.S. bond market, noting significant purchasing power loss in the US dollar over a five-year period.
content_ta: Bitcoin-ன் வெற்றிக்கு வட்டி விகிதக் குறைப்புக்கள் தேவையில்லை என்று ஆய்வாளர் Sam Callahan வாதிடுகிறார். தனது சமீபத்திய ஆய்வில், நிதி அடக்குமுறை, கோர் PCE உயர்வு மற்றும் U.S. பத்திரச் சந்தையின் வீழ்ச்சி பற்றி அவர் விவரித்துள்ளார். மேலும் ஐந்து ஆண்டு காலத்தில் US டாலரின் வாங்கும் திறன் கணிசமாகக் குறைந்துள்ளதாகவும் அவர் குறிப்பிட்டுள்ளார்.

title: Strive Adds 1,223 Bitcoin As Corporate Treasury Reaches 36,818 BTC
summary: TL;DR: Strive purchased another 1,223 Bitcoin over two days, taking its reported holdings to 36,818 BTC in a fresh SEC filing. Strive’s Bitcoin buying spree continued through the middle of October. In a filing dated Monday, the company disclosed the purchase of 1,223 BTC between October 14 and October 16, bringing its total reported holdings to 36,818 coins. The latest purchase cost roughly $100 million at an average price of about $81,734 per Bitcoin, according to the company’s figures. It followed an earlier acquisition of 2,822 BTC in the same week, showing how aggressively the corporate treasury strategy has accelerated. The size of the holding puts Strive among the largest publicly traded Bitcoin owners. That creates an unusual relationship between the company’s shares, its balance sheet and the price of Bitcoin: investors are evaluating not only the coins it holds, but also how management finances future purchases. Preferred shares, equity issuance and other capital-market tools are increasingly central to the treasury-company model. They can give firms more ways to acquire Bitcoin, but also raise questions around funding costs, dilution and the risk of buying into volatile markets. Strive’s announcement does not tell us where Bitcoin prices go next. It does, however, give a clear snapshot of one company’s conviction and the increasing scale of its exposure. The key metric for shareholders will be whether that accumulation creates value per share, not just a larger total Bitcoin balance. Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.
content: Strive has expanded its corporate treasury by purchasing an additional 1,223 Bitcoin over two days, bringing its total holdings to 36,818 BTC. The recent acquisition cost approximately $100 million, reflecting the company's aggressive accumulation strategy. This positions Strive among the largest publicly traded Bitcoin holders, raising important considerations for investors regarding financing methods, potential equity dilution, and overall value creation per share in volatile markets.

title: Reading payment data versus acting on it: why affordability belongs to account information

content: Reading payment data and actually acting upon it are two different concepts in the financial sector. Industry experts argue that proper assessment relies heavily on leveraging account information to make informed decisions, ensuring better financial outcomes and supporting customers effectively in managing their financial health.

title: Google Cloud Outage in London Disrupts Banking and Public Services Across the UK
summary:
A disruption affecting Google Cloud’s London-based infrastructure on October 20 caused technical issues for several banks, financial institutions and public service providers, highlighting the growing reliance on cloud technology across critical services.
Among the affected institutions, UK-based digital bank Revolut experienced service interruptions, with card payments, ATM withdrawals and other services reported as unavailable or partially operational. Germany’s ING also reported difficulties accessing online banking and its mobile application, while Halifax customers encountered problems with digital banking services.
Outage-tracking platform Downdetector recorded reports involving several other organisations, including Lloyds Bank, HSBC, Bank of Scotland, property platform Rightmove, parcel delivery company DPD, NHS England and Royal Mail. The extent of the impact varied across providers, and Lloyds Bank stated that its app remained operational, although some customers were experiencing issues with certain online services.
Google confirmed that its engineering team was investigating the incident affecting its europe-west2 data centre, which primarily serves customers in the UK and Ireland.
Revolut reassured customers about the security of their information and funds, stating: "We can confirm that all our customers' money and data are safe."
The incident also draws attention to growing regulatory scrutiny of financial institutions’ dependence on third-party technology providers. The UK has designated Google Cloud EMEA Limited and three other technology companies as critical third-party suppliers to the financial sector, placing them under direct regulatory oversight. EU regulators have also identified major technology providers whose services are essential to the region’s financial industry.
As banks and public institutions continue to rely on cloud-based infrastructure, the disruption highlights the importance of operational resilience, effective contingency planning and the ability to maintain essential services during technology outages.
Source: Reuters

title: Flex Expands Beyond Rent to Build the Payment Layer for Life’s Financial Obligations
summary:
Flexible Finance, Inc. (“Flex”), the financial technology company building the payment layer for life’s financial obligations, today announced a major expansion of its platform beyond rent. Available immediately, customers can use Flex to manage broadband, car, insurance, mortgage, and utility payments. The expansion builds on a platform that now handles more than $2 billion in payments per month, has served more than 3.5 million customers, and has processed over $45 billion in payments to date. 
Housing and transportation alone—including rent or mortgage, utilities, car payments and insurance—account for roughly half of U.S. consumer spending, or more than $5.3 trillion annually. These payments move through thousands of disconnected apps and websites, each with their own due dates and terms that are often not aligned with paydays, creating a cash-flow challenge no one has solved yet.
“A decade of fintech innovation has transformed almost every part of money management, but it has largely ignored the bills that take up the largest share of household budgets, leaving them fragmented and difficult to manage,” said Shragie Lichtenstein, CEO of Flex. “Rent is where we started, but our vision was always bigger: to build the payment layer for life’s financial obligations and put households back in control of their cash flow."
Today, Flex helps customers avoid more than $39 million in late fees each month and has helped them avoid more than $780 million in total to date. The company applies the same customer-first principles to every bill: transparent pricing, no late fees or penalties charged by Flex, and balances that don’t revolve or compound—plus rent reporting is included to help users build credit history. Before committing, customers see a personalized total based on the bills they choose to pay or split. Pricing includes a $5.99 monthly membership fee and a 0.5% processing fee on all bills paid through Flex. Customers who split a payment also pay a fee of up to 3% of the amount Flex advances. 
The model also creates a more reliable payment relationship between households and billers. By helping billers receive payment in full and on time, Flex can help improve payment performance, reduce the operational burden of collections, and strengthen customer relationships.
Flex's growth is backed by more than $1.5 billion in committed secured borrowing capacity.  If approved, Flex’s bank charter application would allow the company to issue its credit products directly and expand access to its payment solutions through a regulated, FDIC-insured institution.
Consumers can take back control of their cashflow today by downloading the Flex app from the Apple App Store or Google Play. Learn more at getflex.com.

title: Mangopay Expands Local Payout Coverage Across APAC, LATAM and EMEA
summary:
Today, leading global wallet infrastructure provider Mangopay announces the expansion of its local payout capabilities to five additional currencies across APAC, Latin America and EMEA: Australian dollar (AUD), Hong Kong dollar (HKD), Singapore dollar (SGD), Mexican peso (MXN) and Turkish lira (TRY).
The expansion enables platforms to route payouts to sellers, service providers and other beneficiaries through domestic payment rails, rather than relying on international transfers. By enabling payouts in the same currency in which funds are held, platforms can avoid foreign exchange conversions, reduce costs and deliver faster, more locally relevant payout experiences.
As platforms expand internationally, managing payouts across multiple markets can require additional banking relationships, integrations and operational processes. Mangopay's expanded local payout coverage helps simplify this complexity, enabling platforms to manage payouts across more markets through a single global payment infrastructure.
Andy Wiggan, CPO, Mangopay, says: “As businesses expand internationally, the need to navigate different currencies, banking systems and payout requirements can add complexity and cost. Our research found that 37% of enterprise platforms identified country-specific payout restrictions as a compliance challenge, highlighting the operational difficulties businesses face as they scale across markets.
“By expanding our local payout capabilities across APAC, Latin America and EMEA, we're helping platforms simplify how they move funds internationally, reduce their reliance on cross-border transfers and deliver faster, more cost-effective experiences for sellers and service providers.”
Over the past 12 months, Mangopay has processed more than 15,000 payouts worth approximately £61 million (€70 million) across these five currencies combined, demonstrating existing demand for payout services in these markets. The news complements Mangopay's wider global payment infrastructure, including its recently expanded Virtual Accounts offering, which enables platforms to collect funds in 24 currencies.

title: Hyperlayer Secures £19.5M to Help Banks Modernise at Speed Without Replacing Core Systems
summary:
Hyperlayer, the technology company helping banks modernise without replacing their core systems, today announced a £19.5 million follow on investment led by existing investor Flintlock Capital.
The Series A2 round, which also includes participation from Mouro Capital, Susquehanna Private Equity Investments, LLLP, and other existing and new investors, takes Hyperlayer’s total funding to nearly £50 million since October 2025. The investment values the banking technology company at £195 million post money.
Hyperlayer will use the new funding to support growth and innovation across its product, engineering and implementation teams, as well as expansion activity across the US, Europe and Asia-Pacific. Founded in 2023 by former Morgan Stanley colleagues, Rob Rooney and Paul Rolles, Hyperlayer’s technology transforms how, and how fast, banks can modernise without disrupting the core systems that support resilience and compliance. 
As part of the investment, Joe Shamess, Co-Founder and General Partner at Flintlock Capital, will join Hyperlayer’s board of directors.
“We're fortunate to be backed by deep experts in fintech. They've watched us go from a standing start to mandates with global Tier 1 banks in three years. That's what's convinced them to back where the company goes next.” Rob Rooney, Co-Founder and CEO, Hyperlayer.
“Hyperlayer’s promise is clear. Banks, credit unions and other financial institutions must modernise at fintech speed without ripping out the core systems that protect them. A year on, that thesis is proven with world class customers and strong market pull. Leading this round, and joining the board, is us doubling down on where Rob and Paul take the business next." Joe Shamess, Co-Founder and General Partner, Flintlock Capital.
Hyperlayer also announced two leadership changes. Board director Louise Chan and current Chief Operating Officer, becomes Chief Commercial Officer, while Ben Helps, currently Chief Strategy Officer, moves to Chief Operating Officer.
“Both are exceptional colleagues and serious contributors to our success to date. Louise has been closing the deals that prove the model works. Ben has been building the operating discipline and strategy that let us deliver for clients and scale without breaking. These appointments recognise the roles they are already playing as Hyperlayer grows and gathers pace.” Rob Rooney, Co-Founder and CEO, Hyperlayer.

title: The Coinbase allegations expose Bitcoin's corporate governance gap
summary: Corporate adoption of bitcoin will stall as long as companies can't show who controls the money, who approves its movement, or whether it's still there, argues Onramp CEO Michael Tanguma.
content: Recent allegations involving Coinbase have highlighted a significant corporate governance gap in Bitcoin adoption. title: Hyperliquid Policy Center Calls For Five Changes To SEC Crypto Rule
summary: TL;DR: The Hyperliquid Policy Center supports the SEC’s proposed crypto framework but says five changes are needed to make the rules workable for token developers and markets. The Hyperliquid Policy Center has welcomed the US Securities and Exchange Commission‘s attempt to clarify how securities law applies to crypto assets, while warning that details around distributions and trading could still create unnecessary barriers. In a comment published October 19, the group urged the regulator to revise its proposed Regulation Crypto Assets framework in five areas. Its concerns include how administrative steps in token airdrops are treated, how tokens can trade after an exempt distribution, and whether a safe harbour offers clear enough protection once a project has matured. The centre also wants clearer rules for token buybacks and a consistent approach to the interaction between federal exemptions and state securities requirements. The proposals reflect a long-running problem for cryptocurrency developers. A network token may begin life inside a fundraising arrangement, yet eventually circulate in a system where thousands of participants trade and use it without dealing directly with its original issuer. Drawing a line between those stages has been difficult under decades-old securities tests. The SEC’s proposal is intended to offer more predictable treatment, but the consultation process shows that industry participants still disagree about where the boundaries should fall. The advocacy group’s submission is not a regulatory decision. It is one contribution to a rulemaking process whose final outcome will depend on the commission’s response to the evidence and objections it receives. Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.
content: The Hyperliquid Policy Center has welcomed the SEC's proposed framework regarding crypto assets while urging five key changes. The advocacy group warned that rules concerning token airdrops, trading after distributions, safe harbours, token buybacks, and state-federal alignment need revision to avoid creating unnecessary barriers for token developers and markets. The consultation process continues as the regulator reviews industry feedback.

title: Bitmine Ethereum Treasury Tops 6 Million ETH After Another Weekly Purchase
summary: TL;DR: Bitmine says its Ethereum holdings reached approximately 6.04 million ETH after it added 12,535 tokens over the past week. Bitmine Immersion Technologies has pushed its Ethereum treasury past the six-million-token mark, reporting holdings of 6,041,481 ETH as of October 18. The company said it acquired another 12,535 ETH during the preceding week. The size is striking even by corporate crypto-treasury standards. Bitmine describes its position as roughly 4.9% of Ethereum’s circulating supply and says more than five million of its ETH are staked. That staking component matters. Unlike a Bitcoin treasury that generally depends on price movements, a large Ethereum holding can also earn network rewards by participating in validation. Rewards are not risk-free, however, and the economics depend on staking performance, technical operations and protocol conditions. Bitmine valued its wider portfolio of crypto assets, cash, marketable securities and other investments at about $15.1 billion. Its holdings therefore represent a substantial bet on Ethereum as both a long-term asset and a productive network. The company’s disclosure offers investors a clearer look at the scale of that wager, though headline token counts are not the same as shareholder returns. Equity valuation, financing arrangements and the market price of ETH all affect what ownership in the company is ultimately worth. As more listed firms build dedicated crypto treasuries, those distinctions are likely to become increasingly important. Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.
content: Bitmine Immersion Technologies announced its Ethereum treasury has surpassed six million tokens, reaching approximately 6,041,481 ETH after a weekly purchase of 12,535 tokens. The company states this represents about 4.9% of Ethereum's circulating supply, with over five million ETH currently staked to earn network rewards. Bitmine values its total portfolio at roughly $15.1 billion, highlighting a massive corporate bet on the cryptocurrency.

content_ta: Las Vegas நகரில் Money20/20 USA மாநாடு தொடங்கியது. இது stablecoin மற்றும் agent தொழில்நுட்பங்களை மையமாகக் கொண்டு நடைபெற்றது. பணப் பரிமாற்றங்கள் தானாக நடைபெறும் போது, அதற்கான ஆபத்தை இறுதியில் யார் ஏற்பது என்ற முக்கிய கேள்வி முதல் நாள் விவாதங்களில் எழுப்பப்பட்டது.

title: Report States Fintech Funding Cratered in Q3 2026
summary: Fintech funding for private ventures remains robust, but it is not immune to market shifts, especially as dollars compete for the hot artificial intelligence (AI) sector. So far, several reports indicate that global Fintech funding has dropped in 2026, and Crunchbase is now throwing its hat in... Read More
content: A recent report indicates that global fintech funding significantly dropped in the third quarter of 2026. While private venture funding for fintech remains generally robust, the sector faces increased pressure as investment dollars increasingly shift toward the booming artificial intelligence industry. According to data from Crunchbase, the fintech market is not immune to these broader market shifts and heightened competition for capital.
content_ta: 2026 ஆம் ஆண்டின் மூன்றாம் காலாண்டில் உலகளாவிய ஃபின்டெக் நிதி உதவி கணிசமாகக் குறைந்துள்ளதாக ஒரு புதிய அறிக்கை தெரிவிக்கிறது. ஃபின்டெக் நிறுவனங்களுக்கான முதலீடுகள் பொதுவாக வலுவாக இருந்தாலும், ஆர்ட்டிஃபிஷியல் இன்டெல்லிஜென்ஸ் துறையை நோக்கி மூலதனம் மாறுவதால் சந்தையில் அழுத்தம் ஏற்பட்டுள்ளது. Crunchbase தரவுகளின்படி, பரந்த சந்தை மாற்றங்கள் மற்றும் மூலதனப் போட்டியில் இருந்து ஃபின்டெக் சந்தை தப்பவில்லை.

title: Michigan credit union to buy Florida bank
summary: The acquisition of Sarasota’s Gulfside Bank fills a coverage gap between Tampa and Fort Myers for DFCU Financial, which is marking its fourth expansion in the Sunshine State.
content: Michigan-based DFCU Financial is expanding its presence in Florida by acquiring Sarasota’s Gulfside Bank. This strategic purchase bridges a geographic coverage gap between Tampa and Fort Myers, marking the credit union's fourth expansion in the state as it continues to grow its regional footprint and banking services.
content_ta: Michigan-ஐச் சேர்ந்த DFCU Financial நிறுவனம், Sarasota-வில் உள்ள Gulfside Bank-ஐக் கைப்பற்றுவதன் மூலம் Florida-வில் தனது இருப்பை விரிவுபடுத்துகிறது. இந்த மூலோபாயக் கொள்முதல் Tampa மற்றும் Fort Myers இடையே உள்ள புவியியல் இடைவெளியைக் நிரப்புகிறது, இது பிராந்தியத்தில் அதன் கால்தடத்தை தொடர்ந்து வளர்க்கும் இந்த கிரெடிட் யூனியனின் நான்காவது விரிவாக்கமாகும்.
